plan.G: When research closes, compare each tree’s measured and correctness-checked programs, then test useful combinations without assuming gains are additive. Compile, correctness-check, and measure every combination afresh against the geometric-mean kernel-time objective. Independently confirm the final candidate and retain the best confirmed program, using the valid baseline as fallback. Do not launch new research.
plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the main independent opportunities in this all-pairs kernel are reusing source data across target particles, reducing hot-loop arithmetic, and improving output work assignment and launch geometry. Keep these as separate research topics so their effects can be measured distinctly. The supplied valid baseline has three timing repetitions with a mean of about 1.849 ms; no optimized candidate measurements are available yet. The reported target is a GH200 with NVRTC CUDA 12.6.3. The CUDA 12.6.3 Best Practices Guide discusses shared-memory reuse and explicitly calling rsqrtf; these motivate hypotheses, not guaranteed speedups. All candidates must retain the specified interface and correctness across the full required input suite.

children.objective: Explore cooperative shared-memory tiling of source particles in src/nbody_kernel.cu to reuse each loaded source across target threads. Keep the pairwise arithmetic close to the reference to isolate the memory-reuse effect. Handle partial tiles with correct uniform synchronization, cover every output row for every supported N, preserve masses exactly, and use only the permitted source and launch files. Judge candidates by the complete correctness suite and the prescribed timing protocol.

children.objective: With the existing one-target-per-thread work mapping and baseline launch configuration, investigate hot-loop arithmetic changes such as explicit rsqrtf use, algebraically removing target-mass multiply/divide under the stated positive-mass constraint, and eliminating the self-interaction branch where valid. Keep this branch free of shared-memory tiling to isolate arithmetic effects. Validate every transformation against the FP64 oracle, tolerances, nonfinite-output rule, and extreme-mass case; retain only measured improvements.
